question: On 8 December 2023, Portugal sent the Spanish Government and the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA) information on the loss of six containers from the cargo ship Toconao in Portuguese waters, off Viana do Castelo. One of the containers contained plastic pellets. On 3 January 2024, the Spanish Government issued its first official communication to the Government of Galicia to inform it of the provenance and origin of the pellets washing up on the Galician coast. 1.
Did the Spanish Government inform the Commission about the pellets from the Toconao washing up on its northern coast? And if so, when?
Did the Spanish Government inform EMSA about the pellets arriving in Spanish territory?
Does the Commission know if the Spanish Government has informed any other countries, such as its neighbour France, about the possibility of the pellets washing up on their shores?
answer: 1 &2. On 8 December 2023, Portugal reported the incident in question to the Union Maritime Information and Exchange System (SafeSeaNet), hosted by the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA). SafeSeaNet provides for the sharing of information between Member States, including the loss of containers at sea and it was duly activated.

On 8 January 2024, Spain requested assistance for Copernicus satellite imagery to obtain further information on the location of the lost containers in question. Consequently, the Maritime Support Services Contingency Plan was activated and the EMSA and Commission received this information. 3.
The Commission does not hold relevant information on the exchange of information between Member States outside of the Union Maritime Information and Exchange System.
